## Introspection query used

The exact statement. Not a description of it. Someone has to be able to rerun this and
get the same file.

```sql
-- TODO: paste the query
```

*EXAMPLE, postgres:*

```sql
SELECT c.table_name, c.column_name, c.data_type, c.is_nullable,
       pgd.description AS column_comment
FROM information_schema.columns c
LEFT JOIN pg_catalog.pg_statio_all_tables st ON st.relname = c.table_name
LEFT JOIN pg_catalog.pg_description pgd
       ON pgd.objoid = st.relid AND pgd.objsubid = c.ordinal_position
WHERE c.table_schema = 'public'
ORDER BY c.table_name, c.ordinal_position
LIMIT 5000;
```

*EXAMPLE, bigquery. Set `maximum_bytes_billed` on every run:*

```sql
SELECT table_name, column_name, data_type, is_nullable
FROM `nimbus-prod.analytics.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS`
ORDER BY table_name, ordinal_position
LIMIT 5000;
```

*EXAMPLE, mongodb. This is a sample, not a catalog. See the banner below:*

```javascript
db.shipments.aggregate([
  { $sample: { size: 1000 } },
  { $project: { kv: { $objectToArray: "$$ROOT" } } },
  { $unwind: "$kv" },
  { $group: { _id: { f: "$kv.k", t: { $type: "$kv.v" } }, n: { $sum: 1 } } },
  { $sort: { n: -1 } }
])
```

## Listing

One row per column. Keep the column order stable, the hash depends on it.

`Nullable` is `yes` or `no`. `Comment` is the database comment where one exists, or a
note about what the column actually holds where it does not. `Notes` carries anything
an analyst must know before filtering on it.

*EXAMPLE, `public.accounts`, postgres:*

| Column | Type | Nullable | Comment | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | `bigint` | no | Account id | The account grain, per `entities.md` section 1. |
| `name` | `text` | no | Display name | Free text. Do not join on it, see `entities.md` section 4. |
| `plan_type` | `text` | no | `solo`, `team`, `enterprise` | Point in time. Say whether a filter uses window start or end. |
| `is_internal` | `boolean` | yes | Internal account flag | Nullable. NULL means never reviewed. Use `IS NOT TRUE`, not `= FALSE`. Exclusion E-3. |
| `account_type` | `text` | no | `standard`, `demo`, `sandbox` | Exclusion E-4 and E-5. |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` | no | Row insert time | Not form submit time. A 2025-09 backfill inserted 88 rows out of order. |
| `churned_at` | `timestamptz` | yes | Billing cancel date | Added 2026-01. Exclusion E-8. NULL for live accounts. |
| `deleted_at` | `timestamptz` | yes | Soft delete | Rows stay. Exclusion E-9. |
| `stripe_customer_id` | `text` | yes | Stripe customer | Confirmed join, 1 to 1, Stripe is source of truth. |

*EXAMPLE, PostHog events. Event properties are schemaless, so this listing is
sampled and the banner above applies:*

| Column | Type | Nullable | Comment | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `event` | `string` | no | Event name | |
| `timestamp` | `timestamp` | no | Client time, UTC | Client clock. Can be wrong. `$sent_at` is the server time. |
| `distinct_id` | `string` | no | PostHog person key | Not `users.id`. Resolve through person merge, see `entities.md` section 4. |
| `properties.account_id` | `string` | yes | Account id, copied at event time | Stale after an account merge. Map through `account_merges`. |
| `properties.environment` | `string` | yes | `production` or `staging` | Missing before 2025-03-01. Exclusion E-5. |
| `properties.origin` | `string` | yes | `nimbus` or `portal` | rare before 2025-06-11. Added that date. Do not chart across it. |
| `properties.$lib` | `string` | yes | Client library | Server-side libs are backfills, not humans. Exclusion E-7. |
